title: GPX Remove Waypoints Tool: Tracks Stay, Pins Go
description: Remove standalone waypoints from a GPX file with the GPX Remove Waypoints Tool — tracks and routes preserved exactly. Free, local processing.
summary_sentence: For example, a file carrying 40 planning waypoints — trailheads you considered, camps you skipped — downloads with zero <wpt> elements while its recorded track keeps all 2,050 of its points.
quick_answer: The GPX Remove Waypoints Tool deletes the standalone <wpt> waypoint elements from a GPX file while preserving its tracks and routes exactly. Load the file in your browser and download the cleaned copy — the recording without the planning clutter, ready for platforms that plot every pin you ever saved.
steps_intro: Waypoints are the pins. Tracks are the journey. Remove one, keep the other:

body.t: Your planning pins include your home, your car and three maybes. Share the track, not the notebook — the sibling strippers handle
Some platforms render every <wpt> as a permanent map pin. A waypoint-free copy shows the clean route alone.
Waypoints were the intention; the track is the evidence. Archiving the evidence clean is a defensible filing habit.
Seasons of saved places accumulate in device exports. Removing them leaves the tracks that were the point of the file.

examples.label: Example · What a waypoint is (and is not)

body.t: A <wpt> is a standalone saved place — summit, camp, trailhead — stored at the top level of the file, independent of any track. Trackpoints (<trkpt>) may pass the same summit; they are the recording's moments, and this tool never touches them.
Route points (<rtept>) belong to planned routes and also survive — they are structure, not pins. The tool's scope is exactly the top-level <wpt> set, stated so the cleaned file holds no surprises.

popular_table.title: Scope of the removal
popular_table.intro: Three point kinds live in a GPX file; exactly one is removed.
popular_table.note: The edit runs on a browser-side copy; the original file is never modified. Extract waypoints first (the extractor tools in this family) if the pins themselves are worth keeping as their own file.

faq: I only want some waypoints gone.
This tool removes the whole <wpt> set. For surgical removal, a text editor finds each <wpt>…</wpt> block by name — or extract all, delete from the copy, and keep the extraction as the pins file.
Do waypoint names inside tracks survive?
Track and segment names are not waypoints and are untouched — only top-level <wpt> elements are in scope.
Will the file still open everywhere?
Yes — a GPX without waypoints is ordinary GPX 1.1; tracks and routes are the elements readers require.
What about courses and FIT files?
Different formats, different editors — this tool speaks GPX XML. Convert FIT to GPX first if a platform offers it.
In the download, no — in your archive, trivially: the original file never changes, and the cleaned file is a copy.
Their <link> and description children go with the <wpt> element — the whole pin, attachments included, is the unit of removal.
